lessons.title: Reading Nifty and Bank Nifty Skew in Practice

children.text: You now know why skew exists. On a live desk you do not have five minutes each morning to re-derive the leverage effect or reason through crash risk premia from first principles. You need a fast, repeatable read: open the chain, glance at a handful of numbers, and know within seconds whether today's skew looks normal, stretched, or worth a second look. This lesson is that practical routine, for both Nifty and Bank Nifty.

body.text: You do not read skew by staring at forty raw strikes. You read it by tracking a small, consistent set of reference points, ATM and a few standard delta points on each wing, and comparing today's read against recent history and against the other index.

body.label: NSE Live Option Chain
body.description: Pull the live Nifty or Bank Nifty chain directly, including bid, ask, last price and open interest per strike, across all listed expiries.

children.text: For a fast daily read, do not solve the whole surface. Track five points on one expiry: ATM, the 25-delta and 10-delta put, and the 25-delta and 10-delta call, using the delta-solving approach from Chapter 1. Five numbers, checked once a day against yesterday's five numbers, tell you almost everything you need before deciding whether to dig further.

children.text: Nifty vs Bank Nifty: Same Shape, Different Personality

columns.label: Nifty
points: Diversification dampens the impact of any single company's news
Skew driven mainly by broad market crash risk and general portfolio hedging flow
Reacts most to market-wide events: Budget, global risk-off, index-level FPI flows

columns.label: Bank Nifty
points: 12 constituents, concentrated entirely in financial services
A single sector shock, a rate decision, an asset-quality scare, moves the whole index
Skew driven by broad crash risk plus sector-specific event risk layered on top
Reacts most to RBI policy days, bank quarterly results season, regulatory changes for lenders

body.text: In the illustrative read above, Bank Nifty's ATM IV sits above Nifty's, and its 25-delta put-minus-call spread, 19.8% − 17.0% ≈ 2.8 points, is wider than Nifty's, 15.6% − 13.6% = 2.0 points. This is a pattern worth watching for, not a guaranteed daily fact: a 12-stock, single-sector index concentrated in financials tends to carry both higher outright volatility and a steeper skew than a 50-stock, multi-sector index, because there is less internal diversification to smooth away sector-specific tail risk, on top of the same market-wide crash risk both indices share.

body.title: Tracking the daily change
body.prompt: Yesterday, Nifty's 25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV spread was 1.6 percentage points. Today, using the table above, that spread is 15.6% − 13.6%. By how many percentage points did the spread widen?
body.explanation: Today's spread is 15.6% − 13.6% = 2.0 points. Against yesterday's 1.6 points, that is a widening of 2.0 − 1.6 = 0.4 points. A single day's move of this size is worth noting on a daily tracker; Chapter 2's next lesson gives you a formal metric, the risk reversal, to size exactly how large a move like this actually is in context.

children.text: A single day's five-point read means little on its own. Keep a running log and compare today's read against three benchmarks: yesterday, the same weekday last week, and the average over the past 10 to 20 sessions. A skew spread sitting near its recent range is unremarkable. A spread stretching well beyond that range, especially in the days ahead of a scheduled event such as an RBI policy day or the Union Budget, is exactly the structural hedging-demand pattern from the previous lesson showing up in real time.
Common Traps When Reading Live Data

body.title: Why comparing skew across different expiries without adjusting for time is misleading

children.text: A weekly expiry's skew and a monthly expiry's skew are not directly comparable numbers. Near-dated skews are typically steeper in percentage-point terms, for the reasons previewed in Chapter 1: less time for the underlying to drift back if it moves sharply, so the market prices tail risk more aggressively per unit of time. If you compare a Tuesday weekly's put-call spread against a far monthly's spread and conclude the weekly skew is 'worse,' you may just be comparing two different points on the term structure. Always compare like tenor to like tenor, this week against last week's same-tenor expiry, not across expiries. Chapter 3 formalizes this comparison properly.

body.text: Far-dated Bank Nifty strikes and deep 10-delta or 5-delta wings on either index can trade on stale prints with almost no volume for hours. Before trusting a five-point read, check that each of the five strikes has traded recently and carries meaningful open interest. A skew spread built on one fresh quote and one four-hour-old stale print is not measuring today's market, it is measuring a data quality problem.

body.title: Two reads, one surprising number
body.scenario: On a routine morning, your five-point tracker shows Nifty's skew spread sitting right at its 20-day average, unremarkable. Bank Nifty's skew spread, however, has widened by 1.8 points overnight, well outside its recent range, with no RBI policy day, results season, or other scheduled banking-sector event on the calendar this week.
body.prompt: What would you check before concluding this is a genuine, tradeable repricing of Bank Nifty sector risk?
body.modelAnswer:
1. First rule out a data problem, exactly as the trap above describes: check that the specific 25-delta and 10-delta strikes driving the move have traded recently and carry normal open interest, not a stale print on a thin far-wing strike.
2. Check whether a single large institutional order, a block hedge or a large FPI put purchase, moved one or two strikes without reflecting a broader shift in market view. A single sizable trade can distort a five-point read for a session without being a genuine sector-wide repricing.
3. Check bank-specific news outside the standard scheduled calendar: a rating action, a large NPA disclosure, a regulatory circular, or global banking-sector stress that would not show up as 'RBI policy day' but is still a real bank-sector risk event.
4. Cross-check against Nifty's own financial-services-heavy constituents and against individual large bank stocks' own option skews, to see whether this is isolated to Bank Nifty specifically or part of a broader financials move that just has not shown up in the broad-index Nifty read yet because banks are only part of that basket.
5. Only once data quality, one-off flow and genuine news are ruled in or out does the widening become a usable signal, either to fade as likely to mean-revert if it looks like noise, or to respect as new information if it survives all four checks.

body.title: Comparing across tenors
body.question: You want to know whether Nifty's put skew is unusually steep today. Which comparison is valid?
options: Today's weekly expiry skew against today's monthly expiry skew
Today's weekly expiry skew against last week's weekly expiry skew at a similar days-to-expiry point
Today's ATM IV against today's 10-delta put IV, treated as a single number
Today's Nifty skew against today's Bank Nifty skew, treated as directly equivalent
body.explanation: Skew readings are only comparable across matching tenor. Comparing a weekly against a same-tenor weekly from a prior period holds time-to-expiry roughly constant, isolating the actual change in skew. Comparing across expiries, collapsing multiple points into one undifferentiated number, or comparing two structurally different indices as if they were interchangeable all mix in effects that have nothing to do with a genuine change in skew.

cards.definition: A practical daily skew snapshot using ATM, 25-delta put, 10-delta put, 25-delta call and 10-delta call IV on one expiry, instead of solving the full surface each time.
NSE's official end-of-day settlement report, used to build historical skew series for backtesting without needing your own live tick capture.
Comparing a skew reading only against another reading at a similar days-to-expiry point, since near-dated and far-dated skews are not directly comparable.
The added skew and volatility a narrow, single-sector index like Bank Nifty carries relative to a broad, multi-sector index like Nifty, due to less internal diversification.

points: Read skew practically using a five-point snapshot, ATM plus 25-delta and 10-delta on each wing, tracked daily rather than re-solving the full surface each morning.
NSE's live option chain gives real-time data you must capture yourself for history; Bhavcopy gives official end-of-day data ready-made for backtesting.
Bank Nifty's sector concentration in financials typically gives it both higher outright IV and a steeper skew than the broader, more diversified Nifty.
Only compare skew readings against the same tenor over time, weekly against weekly, monthly against monthly, since near-dated and far-dated skews are not directly comparable.
Before trusting a skew reading, check that the strikes driving it have actually traded recently with real open interest, especially on far wings and longer-dated Bank Nifty expiries.
An unusual skew reading needs a process, ruling out data problems and one-off flow before treating it as genuine new information, not an instant trading signal.
